caption: Characteristics of the two validation cohorts and of the Mayo Clinic cohort in which the Leibovich score was developed (Leibovich et al., 2003). Values are n (%) unless stated. Predictors are as recorded, before imputation; unknown nodal status (pNx) is counted with pN0, as in the score, and risk groups are given only for patients with all five predictors. Follow-up starts at randomisation in TranSORCE and at surgery in the Vasudev cohort, and events are counted over all follow-up. The event is distant metastasis in TranSORCE and any relapse in the Vasudev cohort. SD, standard deviation.

Performance of the Leibovich model and Leibovich Plus at 5 years. In TranSORCE, follow-up starts at randomisation and the event is distant metastasis; in the Vasudev cohort, follow-up starts at surgery and the event is any relapse. Observed incidence is the Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence of the event, with death without the event as the competing event. Intervals are 95% bootstrap percentile intervals. Relapse includes every distant metastasis, so an O/E below 1 in the Vasudev cohort shows over-prediction, but one above 1 does not show under-prediction. The other-cause O/E compares the observed incidence of death without the event with Leibovich Plus's predicted other-cause risk; it is marked descriptive in TranSORCE, which had few such deaths. O/E, observed-to-expected ratio; ICI, integrated calibration index; AUC, time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve.

Flow of patients into the analysis sets of TranSORCE (A) and the Vasudev cohort (B). RELAPSE and DFS_STATUS are source fields of the Vasudev cohort. DFS, disease-free survival; M1, distant metastasis at diagnosis.

Calibration of predicted 5-year risk. Lines are smoothed calibration curves; points are fifths of predicted risk with 95% bootstrap percentile intervals. The dashed line marks perfect calibration, and the ticks at the foot of each panel show the spread of each model's predicted risk. In TranSORCE, follow-up starts at randomisation, the event is distant metastasis and predictions are conditional on being event-free at randomisation. In the Vasudev cohort, follow-up starts at surgery and the event is any relapse. Death without the event is the competing event in both. Relapse includes every distant metastasis, so in B a point below the dashed line shows over-prediction but a point above it does not show under-prediction.

Observed and predicted 5-year risk by age at surgery. In the bottom row, observed death without the event is set against Leibovich Plus's predicted other-cause risk; the original Leibovich model does not estimate this risk. Observed values are Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidences with 95% bootstrap percentile intervals. Hatched rows have fewer than 10 events. Follow-up, events and the competing event are as in Figure 2.
Rules that map each cohort's source fields to the predictors, outcomes and design fields used in the analysis, with the handling of missing values.

Classification of every distinct entry in the TranSORCE free-text "Other: Details" field. Only distant_metastasis counts as the event. Flagged entries needed clinical review; laterality marks entries whose class depends on which kidney was removed.

Specification of the validated models: the Leibovich coefficients and score points with their sources, the tumour profiles of Stimpson et al., the recovered baseline cumulative hazard and the life-table settings.
Missing predictor values before imputation, and the imputation model. Unrecorded nodal status is not imputed; it scores as pN0.

Observed and predicted risk of death without the event under Leibovich Plus, overall and by age at surgery, at 3 and 5 years. Observed incidence is the Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence with its 95% bootstrap percentile interval. Groups with fewer than 10 deaths are flagged as few events. TranSORCE rows are descriptive. O/E, observed-to-expected ratio.
Performance of the Leibovich model and Leibovich Plus at 3 years, laid out as Table 2.

Predicted cumulative incidence of distant metastasis in men for the three tumour profiles of Stimpson et al., defined in Table S2. The original Leibovich model does not use age, so it has one curve per profile. Leibovich Plus divides the risk of either event in proportion to the two cumulative risks, so its predicted risk can fall as follow-up lengthens, as in the high-risk profile at older ages.

Observed and predicted 5-year risk of the event by Leibovich risk group (low, score 0 to 2; intermediate, 3 to 5; high, 6 or more). SORCE enrolled only patients with a score of 3 or more, so TranSORCE has no low-risk group. Group sizes and event counts in the Vasudev cohort are averages over the imputed datasets. Symbols, intervals and hatching are as in Figure 3; follow-up, events and the competing event as in Figure 2.
